d.d: Nearest in place or position, having nothing similar intervening; adjoining.
d.x: The man in the next bunk kept me awake all night with his snoring.

d.d: Nearest in order, succession, or rank; immediately following (or sometimes preceding) in order.
d.x: Please turn to the next page.

d.d: Nearest in relationship. (See also next of kin.)
Denotes the one immediately following the current or most recent one.
d.x: Next week would be a good time to meet.

d.d: Closest in the future, or closest but one if the closest is very soon; of days, sometimes thought to specifically refer to the instance closest to seven days (one week) in the future.
d.x: The party is next Tuesday; that is, not tomorrow, but eight days from now.

d.d: In a time, place, rank or sequence closest or following.
d.x: They live in the next closest house.

d.d: So as to follow in time or sequence something previously mentioned.

d.x: Financial panic, earthquakes, oil spills, riots. What comes next?

d.d: The one that follows after this one.
d.x: Next, please, don't hold up the queue!

d.d: A form or state of connection.
The relationship between a vendor and a jurisdiction for the purpose of taxation, established for example by the vendor operating a physical store in that jurisdiction.
A connected group; a network, a web.
